The Executive Director will assume full operational leadership of a high\-impact nonprofit team, managing programmatic execution, facility partnership integration at Squash Zone, and working in close alignment with the Board of Directors to achieve fundraising, compliance, and multi\-year strategic growth goals.

Students in the program learn how to play squash, receive academic and other support tailored to their needs, and become part of a supportive community centered at Squash Zone, a state\-of\-the\-art squash center with nine squash courts and dedicated academic space. With an operating budget of $350,000, Squash on Track enrolls approximately 20 elementary and middle school students and aims to expand to at least 40 students by 2028\.

* ● Manage and run the daily **youth program** in a manner which ensures exceptionalprogramming, maximum enrollment, and excellent attendance, in\-year and longitudinalretention.
* ● Lead a comprehensive **development/fundraising** effort to build the financial assets of theorganization by raising an annual surplus and undertaking capital and endowmentcampaigns as required.
* ● Lead and develop SoT **personnel** to ensure the attraction, development, and retention oftop talent and longevity of leadership within the organization.
* ● Oversee, manage, and maintain the organization’s **physical assets and facility needs**.
* ● Oversee all matters of **fiscal and legal compliance** for the organization, ensuringcomprehensive “good standing.”
* ● Develop the **Board of Directors** and work closely with them to build the organization.

**Job Description**  

New York City Emergency Management (NYCEM) helps New Yorkers before, during, and after emergencies through preparedness, education, and response. NYCEM is responsible for coordinating citywide emergency planning and response for all types and scales of emergencies. We are staffed by more than 200 dedicated professionals with diverse backgrounds and areas of expertise, including individuals assigned from other City agencies.  

  

The Office of the Chief Counsel provides legal advice to NYCEM executives and staff regarding critical, strategic, legal and policy issues facing the agency, engages in transactional work in support of the NYCEM mission and coordinates with the NYC Law Department, Office of the Chief Counsel to the Mayor and City Hall, and other local, state and federal counsels regarding various legal issues ranging from emergency events to litigation, which impact the agency. The Office of Chief Counsel is comprised of the Legal Affairs Unit, the Civil and Human Rights Unit formerly known as the Disability, Access and Functional Needs Unit (DAFN), and the Records Management Unit.  

  

The Records Management Unit is responsible for leading and managing the NYCEM records management program. It develops and implements policies and procedures to manage agency records throughout their life cycle, from creation to their final disposition, and works with units and personnel to ensure all staff are aware of and can apply records management best practices into their daily course of business.  

  

The Office of the Chief Counsel is seeking a Deputy Director of Records who will oversee work of the Records Management unit and supervise the Records Program Manager and any temporary staff, including interns. The Deputy Director of Records will oversee the maintenance and management the agency’s electronic and physical records. This includes any day\-to\-day responsibilities and creating and implementing policies around agency records. The Deputy Director of Records will work with staff to ensure that all records are in compliance according to City policies and procedures.  

  

Under the supervision of the Chief Counsel, the Deputy Director of Records will have responsibilities including but not limited to the following:  

  

* Overseeing Records Management unit staff and interns.
* Managing and maintaining an electronic records management system, currently RecordPoint’s Records365\.
* Performing day\-to\-day records management tasks and activities relating to storage, retrieval, retention and disposition of records.
* Training staff in the procedures related to policies governing the maintenance of all documents (both records and non\-records, regardless of format) and ensuring staff are aware of their role in the management of agency records.
* Overseeing all Records Management unit functions and projects including but not limited to reviewing and updating the retention schedule as needed, applying retention to records in SharePoint using Records365, creating destruction and transfer requests, choosing a system to manage physical records (potentially Records365\).
* Developing and implementing agency records management policies and related procedures as needed and performing yearly reviews and updates of established policies.
* Creating one page infographics to communicate important policies or procedures to NYCEM staff as needed.
* Overseeing all scanning projects which must follow the NYC Department of Records and Information Services’ (DORIS) processes and guidelines and be approved by DORIS before projects may commence. Potential scanning projects include eligible agency records with long\-term retention periods or special scanning projects (e.g., activation records to be transferred to another City agency).
* Maintaining filing system procedures and classification indexes.
* Assigning and managing file space as well as inventorying boxes and preparing materials for storage or transfer to the NYC Municipal Records Center if needed.
* Working with staff to ensure all agency publications that are required to be submitted to the NYC Municipal Library are transferred to the Records Management unit for submission to the Library’s Government Publications Portal.
* Choosing, inventorying and cataloging materials in the agency library and managing patrons and the circulation of the collection utilizing ResourceMate Plus.

**About Back to the Bible**

Back to the Bible is an 87\-year\-old ministry that exists to help everyone, everywhere know, love, and be transformed by God's Word. Founded in 1939, the organization served as a radio ministry through 2020 before entering a new chapter built around digital biblical content and Bible engagement research.

The ministry does two things well: producing daily biblical content and conducting transformative research at the Center for Scripture Absorption. Since 2025 it has experienced renewed momentum, growing its YouTube audience to more than 130,000 subscribers, and the CSA undertaking research projects on a global scale. The organization is moving quickly and changing fast.

**About the Role**

Back to the Bible is looking for an experienced fundraising leader to build the strategy, systems, and rhythm behind a development operation entering a season of renewed momentum. Over the past year the ministry has stabilized and rebuilt its operations \& focused heavily on renewing \& expanding its donor base. The Director of Development will take that foundation and operationalize it.

The ministry carries a rich legacy and a large existing donor base. Roughly one third of revenue comes from planned and estate gifts, one third from major donors, and one third from general donors. Appeals and newsletters already generate a strong response and have real room to perform better. Digital fundraising is largely untapped beyond a monthly email appeal and a digital newsletter, even as the ministry's digital audience grows rapidly.

This role is split roughly in half. One half is designing and running the annual giving program: appeals, newsletters, monthly donor acquisition, digital fundraising, donor journey and appreciation, and reactivation of lapsing donors. The other half is direct donor work: carrying a portfolio, upgrading donors with the capacity to give more, and meeting with supporters in person where it is strategic.

The Executive Director remains highly active in fundraising, particularly in new major donor cultivation. The Director of Development will work alongside a major gifts officer and a donor relations coordinator and will partner closely with the Directional Leadership Team on organizational fundraising priorities.

* Create a donor journey and appreciation strategy that measurably improves retention
* Identify lapsing donors and design reactivation campaigns

**Donor Portfolio and Major Gifts**

* Identify and qualify new prospects using wealth screening and data analysis
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward gifts, tailoring outreach to each donor's connection to the mission
* Visit donors in person where appropriate and strategic

Irvine Nature Center seeks a strategic, entrepreneurial, and results\-oriented Director of Advancement to lead all fundraising, marketing, communications, and revenue\-generation efforts for the organization.

This role oversees all fundraising activities, including major gifts, annual giving, corporate and foundation partnerships, planned giving, stewardship, special events, and the completion of Irvine’s $10 million capital campaign. The Director of Advancement will serve as a strategic partner to the Executive and Deputy Directors and help build a modern, high\-performing Office of Advancement that aligns fundraising, marketing, communications, and audience development strategies to drive organizational growth.

The Advancement team currently includes three full\-time fundraising staff members, with funding available for the successful candidate to evaluate future staffing structure and departmental growth.

The ideal candidate is a highly motivated revenue\-builder who combines strategic leadership with hands\-on execution and has a proven ability to grow fundraising results, expand audiences, and drive engagement through effective marketing and relationship management.

Key Responsibilities

Advancement Strategy \& Revenue Growth

Develop and lead a comprehensive advancement strategy focused on increasing philanthropic and earned revenue.

Partner with the Executive Director and Board of Trustees to establish fundraising priorities, revenue goals, and growth strategies.

Build and strengthen a culture of philanthropy and revenue accountability across the organization.

Track and analyze fundraising, marketing, attendance, and engagement metrics to drive decision\-making and performance.

Founded in 2013, Young Musicians Unite (YMU) provides free, high\-quality music education to students in under\-resourced communities across Miami\-Dade County. Through deep partnerships with public schools, YMU reaches more than 16,000 students across 105 schools, with an annual operating budget of approximately $9 million. YMU is known for ambitious growth, strong school and community partnerships, large\-scale fundraising efforts, and a highly entrepreneurial culture. **Position Overview**

Young Musicians Unite is seeking an accomplished Chief Operating Officer to lead the organization's internal operations and help build the management infrastructure required to sustain rapid growth.

Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO will serve as YMU's senior operating executive and a central member of the executive leadership team. The COO will oversee organizational execution, leadership team management, finance and administrative oversight, people systems, cross\-functional coordination, organizational planning, performance management, and the systems and processes that enable YMU to operate effectively at scale.

YMU operates on the Entrepreneurial Operating System (EOS), and the COO will serve in the organization's Integrator role. Prior EOS experience is preferred but not required. What matters most is a demonstrated ability to perform the work of an exceptional Integrator.

This is a broad organizational leadership role designed for an experienced executive who has successfully led within an organization of comparable or greater complexity.

The COO will strengthen how YMU operates, develop its leaders, clarify accountability, improve organizational visibility, and build the infrastructure required for continued growth.

The COO must also preserve the qualities that have enabled YMU to grow: entrepreneurial thinking, speed, creativity, resourcefulness, strong relationships, and commitment to the mission.

***Success in this role means a stronger, more accountable, coordinated, financially disciplined organization that can scale without sacrificing quality or culture.*** 

**Core Responsibilities**

* Serve as YMU's senior operating leader and EOS Integrator, translating strategy into execution.
* Lead and develop the senior leadership team, creating clear ownership, accountability, and high performance.
* Own YMU's EOS operating cadence, including planning, Rocks, scorecards, Level 10 Meetings, issue solving, and follow\-through.
* Strengthen organizational structure, management, talent planning, and performance management as YMU grows.
* Oversee finance in partnership with the Controller and CEO, including budgeting, forecasting, financial performance, risk, and resource allocation.
* Ensure YMU's people, administrative, compliance, and core operating functions are reliable and well managed.
* Drive cross\-functional coordination and resolve unclear ownership, competing priorities, bottlenecks, and execution problems.
* Build simple, scalable systems that improve performance without unnecessary bureaucracy.
* Maintain clear visibility into organizational performance and surface important risks, issues, and decisions early.
* Serve as a trusted operating partner to the CEO and support the Board with clear operational and financial reporting.

**Qualifications** 

Required Experience \& Skills

* 10\+ years of progressive leadership experience, including significant senior executive responsibility.
* Demonstrated success scaling an organization of comparable or greater size and complexity.
* Experience in a COO, President, Executive Director, Managing Director, or similarly broad leadership role.
* Significant experience managing senior leaders and building high\-performing teams. Proven record of improving organizational execution, management, systems, or performance.
* Strong financial and business acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, planning, and resource allocation.
* Proven ability to create clarity, accountability, and effective systems in a fast\-moving organization.
* Excellent judgment, problem\-solving, decision\-making, and communication skills.
* High integrity, maturity, and ability to build trust with employees, executives, board members, and external partners.

Preferred Background

* Experience with EOS, particularly as an Integrator or senior leadership team member.
* Experience scaling a rapidly growing organization.
* Experience in an entrepreneurial or founder\-led environment. Experience leading a multi\-site, distributed\-workforce, education, service\-delivery, or similarly complex organization.
* Experience working with boards of directors.
* Experience in nonprofit, education, youth development, arts, or another mission\-driven field.
* Success improving systems, processes, data visibility, and technology.

*Nonprofit experience is preferred but not required. YMU welcomes proven leaders from the private, public, and nonprofit sectors who have successfully led complex organizations.*

The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and 182 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org


**VPU Context:**The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) is a shared commitment to end the world’s learning crisis. It is the only global partnership and fund dedicated entirely to helping children in lower\-income countries get a quality education, so they can unlock their potential and contribute to building a better world.


We bring together governments, teachers, civil society, donors, United Nations agencies, development banks, businesses and private foundations to transform education systems so that every girl and boy can have hope, opportunity and agency.


**What We Do**


GPE helps low\- and lower\-middle\-income countries build stronger education systems so that all children can get the education they need to thrive. We support more than 90 countries where the needs are greatest and focus on reaching the children who are the most vulnerable, including girls, children with disabilities, and those affected by extreme poverty or conflict. Our unique approach works. Between 2021 and 2025, GPE supported 372 million children in partner countries to get a better education through grants and co\-financing.


**How We Work**


GPE is working to help governments transform their education systems to get the most vulnerable children in school, improve teaching and learning, and build equitable, inclusive and resilient education systems fit for the 21st century. Transforming education is about creating lasting changes and achieving impact on a scale. GPE sets out to deliver this transformative change by convening partners, mobilizing funds and catalyzing reforms to help partner countries accelerate access, learning outcomes and gender equality.


**Multiply Possibility – Financing GPE 2030**


GPE launched its 5th financing campaign for 2026\-2030, co\-hosted by Italy and Nigeria, to mobilize $5 billion for inclusive, high\-performing education systems in the world’s most challenging contexts. A fully funded GPE will transform education systems and multiply possibility for 750 million children in 96 countries.

The GPE Board of Directors includes ministerial\-level board members and alternates representing 20 constituencies that reflect the partnership’s breadth. The Board Chair is H.E. The American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) seeks a dynamic, growth\-oriented science policy leader to take the Center for Scientific Evidence in Public Issues (EPI Center) (https://www.aaas.org/programs/epi\-center) into its next phase.


The EPI Center bolsters public decisions about the most important issues of our day by facilitating scientific evidence’s inclusion in a complex process through high\-touch, high\-context dialogue and resources.



The EPI Center advances evidence\-informed decision making by:


* Bringing policy\-relevant, unbiased, non\-partisan scientific evidence to public decisionmakers at all levels of government;
* Facilitating multi\-sector and multi\-stakeholder engagements (virtual and in\-person) to build trusted relationships between scientists and policymakers to deliver clear, actionable, and timely information to the people who need it most.


The Center's collaborative engagement model leverages partnerships with nationally recognized civic intermediaries—including the National Governors Association, the National League of Cities, the National Conference of State Legislatures, and the Council of State Governments—to reach state and local decision\-makers across the political spectrum. To date, EPI Center projects have reached over 10,000 decision\-makers, including officials in every state, U.S. territory, and Washington, DC, enabling policymakers to more easily access, understand and incorporate scientific expertise into their decision\-making.


*Help us ignite the next era of science.*

  


**What You’ll Do**



As the Center enters the next phase of its growth, the **Director of the EPI Center** has ultimate responsibility for setting the Center’s long\-term strategy and overseeing its day\-to\-day operations, leading a high\-performing team of professionals and an ever\-growing network of collaborators. This position reports to the AAAS Chief Program Officer, and the EPI Center is situated in the programmatic arm of AAAS. The Director will drive the Center’s fundraising in close collaboration with the AAAS Advancement team and build support for the EPI Center with a wide range of public stakeholders. The Director oversees the Center’s budgetary and financial management; represents AAAS broadly; and continually identifies topics for which scientific evidence and connection to scientists is relevant to policymakers. Responsibilities include:


* Serves as an energetic team leader, determining overall priorities, continually refining the EPI Center value proposition in a complex and rapidly changing policy ecosystem.
* Serves as the primary champion and external face for the program, to include building partnerships with civic intermediary organizations, relevant policymakers and their professional staff, scientists and scientific organizations, and existing and prospective funders.
* Leads fundraising strategy and activities in close consultation with and with support from the AAAS Office of Advancement, including identifying and engaging prospective funders, soliciting funding (including grant and contract writing), and managing funder relationships.
* Takes primary program\-level responsibility for budget, grants, and personnel management. Serves as top manager of all Center employees, overseeing program\-level personnel considerations and decisions including hiring, training, promotions, assessments, and short\- and long\-term adjustments to duties as needed to ensure programmatic success and continuity of operations. * Takes overarching responsibility for the content, accuracy, and tone of all public\-facing communications. * Collaborate and coordinate across AAAS programs to build multi\-audience and multi\-stakeholder engagement approaches that optimize effective use of resources and advance the use of science in public decision\-making.
* Additional duties as assigned.

Back to the Bible is an 87\-year\-old ministry that exists to help everyone, everywhere know, love, and be transformed by God's Word. Founded in 1939, the organization served as a radio ministry through 2020 before entering a new chapter built around digital biblical content and Bible engagement research.

The ministry does two things well: producing daily biblical content and conducting transformative research at the Center for Scripture Absorption. Since 2025 it has experienced renewed momentum, growing its YouTube audience to more than 130,000 subscribers, and the CSA undertaking research projects on a global scale. The organization is moving quickly and changing fast.

**About the Role**

Back to the Bible is looking for an experienced fundraising leader to build the strategy, systems, and rhythm behind a development operation entering a season of renewed momentum. Over the past year the ministry has stabilized and rebuilt its operations \& focused heavily on renewing \& expanding its donor base. The Director of Development will take that foundation and operationalize it.

The ministry carries a rich legacy and a large existing donor base. Roughly one third of revenue comes from planned and estate gifts, one third from major donors, and one third from general donors. Appeals and newsletters already generate a strong response and have real room to perform better. Digital fundraising is largely untapped beyond a monthly email appeal and a digital newsletter, even as the ministry's digital audience grows rapidly.

**OVERVIEW**


The Senior Director of Development provides strategic and organizational leadership for Mercy Street's fundraising efforts and is responsible for building and executing a comprehensive development strategy that provides the resources necessary to advance Mercy Street's mission and growth.


The Senior Director leads the entire Development Department, establishes fundraising strategy and accountability, develops staff, partners closely with the President \& CEO, and ensures that major gifts, foundations, annual giving, events, donor stewardship, development operations, and other revenue strategies function as one coordinated fundraising effort.

**DEVELOPMENT LEADERSHIP \& STRATEGY**


* Develop and lead Mercy Street's annual and multi\-year fundraising strategy.
* Translate organizational revenue goals into clear fundraising plans, strategies, assignments, and measurable outcomes.
* Maintain overall accountability for achieving contributed\-revenue goals.
* Lead and develop the Development team.
* Establish clear priorities and accountability across major gifts, grants and foundations, operations, annual giving, events, and stewardship.
* Lead regular Development team meetings and performance reviews.
* Build a culture of excellence, collaboration, accountability, stewardship, and continuous improvement.

**REVENUE STRATEGY**


* Maintain visibility into the entire fundraising pipeline.
* Monitor performance against annual goals and make strategic adjustments when revenue is behind plan.
* Ensure Mercy Street maintains a healthy mix of individual, foundation, corporate, church, event, and other contributed revenue.

* Manage the CEO's development involvement strategically rather than operationally.
* Help determine which donors and prospects require CEO engagement.

* Follow up on CEO donor activity so relationships continue moving forward after meetings.

* Directly supervise and coach the Director of Major Gifts, Director of Grants \& Foundations, and Director of Development Operations.
* Establish goals and performance expectations for each development function.
* Resolve competing priorities across development.
* Ensure strong collaboration instead of functional silos.
* Identify future staffing and capacity needs as Mercy Street grows.

**EXECUTIVE \& BOARD LEADERSHIP**


* Provide development updates to executive leadership and the Board as requested.
* Partner with board members in donor cultivation and introductions.
* Help strengthen the Board's fundraising engagement.
* Participate in organizational planning and budgeting.

* Serve on appropriate committees; attend staff meetings, and other staff functions.
* Strengthen teamwork, collaboration, alignment, morale, transparency, credibility, and trust throughout the ministry.
* Fulfill necessary tasks, projects or roles as assigned.

We realize exceptional people don't choose roles based solely on benefits, but we do our best to make sure that our team is set up for success so that they can do their best work. We want to ensure the sustainability of each employee, considering the difficulty of our work and our desire for each staff member to carry out our mission to the fullest extent possible.
